Per this lore, he is a particularly stupid villager who gets married off to an intelligent princess because of the scheming of a spurned courtier. The princess asks her new husband, “_asti kaschit vAgviSEshah_?” (“is there any special erudition within you?”), which he promptly fails to understand. After some intense melodrama and divine intervention by Kali, he becomes a great poet, and he decides to compose works beginning with each of those taunting words. The Erdős number describes the "collaborative distance" between mathematician Paul Erdős and another person, as measured by authorship of mathematical papers. A number of variations on the concept have been proposed to apply to other fields, notably the Bacon number, connecting actors to the actor Kevin Bacon by a chain of joint appearances in films. A small number of people are connected to both Erdős and Bacon and thus have an Erdős–Bacon number, which combines the two numbers by taking their sum.
Even further extension has been made possible. For example, the "Erdős–Bacon–X number" is the sum of the Erdős–Bacon number and the collaborative distance to X in terms of singing in public.

X = Consistent word spacing Y = Writing / script Writing long predates medieval Europe, but routine, consistent word spacing is relatively late. Insular manuscripts (Ireland & Britain, 7th–9th c.) are where systematic spacing first appears. Classical Greek & Latin used _scriptio continua_, with spacing only used sporadically for novices. Scholars fluent in the language didn’t need spacing; Irish monks learning Latin did, so they innovated. Spacing later proved to speed silent reading and reduce copying errors, spreading across Europe.
